extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers interested in the Steele dossier and intelligence/investigative standards
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the reliability, evidentiary value, and investigatory role of an intelligence-style dossier (here, the Steele dossier), including source credibility, corroboration, legal uses (e.g., FISA), and how media and agencies should treat unverified raw intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for independent corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations in the Steele election reports 'could not be corroborated' and the FBI was 'not able to corroborate a single substantive allegation contained in the Steele Reports' despite protracted efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should seek independent evidence (time, location, participants) to verify memos' claims; public reporting should note when corroboration is absent. CNN and U.S. officials later corroborated some specific communications (same individuals, same days, same locations) — demonstrating the type of independent checks that increase confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess source credibility and past reporting record
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate Intelligence Committee criticized the FBI for giving Steele's allegations 'unjustified credence' based on an incomplete understanding of Steele's past reporting record; investigators examined Steele and his 'vast network' and judged sources credible in some instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a source's past accuracy and tendencies (e.g., Steele described a subsource as a 'boaster' and 'egoist' who 'may engage in some embellishment'); adjust weight given to reporting accordingly and disclose such caveats when using the reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat raw intelligence with skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers warned that 'nobody should believe something just because an intelligence agent says it' and that raw intelligence is 'still treated with skepticism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw intel, even from respected agents, should be investigated further rather than accepted at face value; intelligence summaries to policymakers can reflect seriousness without equating to verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine possibility of deliberate disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: The IG report concluded 'more should have been done to examine Steele's contacts with intermediaries of Russian oligarchs ... to assess those contacts as potential sources of disinformation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators must consider whether sources or intermediaries could be vectors for foreign disinformation campaigns and factor that risk into assessment and corroboration efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose caveats about source reliability in legal filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Steele provided 'caveats about his source' that the FBI omitted from its FISA application; the IG report criticized lack of transparency about sourcing quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using intelligence reporting in legal or court filings (e.g., FISA applications), explicitly include known limitations or caveats about source reliability so decision-makers can weigh the information appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of reporting in meeting legal probable-cause standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The IG report said the Steele reporting 'pushed [the FISA proposal] over the line' in terms of establishing probable cause for a FISA on Carter Page; other officials said it was 'a smart part' of the evidence but not the majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether and how unverified reporting contributes to satisfying statutory/legal thresholds (e.g., probable cause), and document which items provided independent evidentiary weight versus merely supplementing other lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing the factual origin/timing of investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple official findings concluded the dossier did not trigger the opening of the Crossfire Hurricane investigation; the real trigger was Papadopoulos-related information and WikiLeaks disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the investigatory timeline with documentary evidence to avoid conflating later-acquired material with the initial basis for opening inquiries; use official records/IG reports to establish causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate core narratives from salacious, unverified details
rubrics_metrics.description: While the most salacious allegations haven't been verified, the dossier's broad assertion that Russia waged a campaign to interfere in the election is now accepted as fact by the US intelligence community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate evaluation of high-level themes (e.g., campaign interference) from investigation of specific sensational claims; give different evidentiary standards and be explicit about which layer is corroborated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic presentation of unverified material
rubrics_metrics.description: News outlets reported the dossier as 'explosive, but largely unverified' and urged 'skepticism and caution'; outlets explicitly noted unsubstantiated status when covering it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media should clearly label unverified intelligence as such, report caveats, and avoid presenting raw allegations as established facts; when possible, report whether specific elements have been corroborated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of political/funding bias vs. evidentiary merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Trump and supporters challenged the dossier's veracity because it was funded in part by the Clinton campaign and DNC; Democrats argued funding source is irrelevant to factual accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between provenance/funding of opposition research and the factual merit of its content; note funding but evaluate claims on evidentiary grounds rather than guilt-by-association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative best practice: try to prove or disprove every assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Bill Priestap said: 'We went to great lengths to try to independently verify the source's credibility and to prove or disprove every single assertion in the dossier.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative teams should attempt systematic verification or falsification of reported assertions rather than treating the dossier as presumptively true or false, documenting efforts and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge classification limits on public verification
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases, public verification is hindered because the information is classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classification prevents public corroboration, explicitly state this limitation and, where possible, provide declassified summaries or explain what cannot be shared and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of corroboration from multiple independent sources
rubrics_metrics.description: A House Intelligence Committee minority report and others stated that 'multiple independent sources ... corroborated Steele's reporting' and that corroboration increased confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent corroboration from separate sources materially increases confidence in claims; documentation should show independence of corroborating lines (different collectors, methods, or records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressing confidence probabilistically
rubrics_metrics.description: Steele said he believes 70–90% of the dossier is accurate and assigned a 50% chance to a specific allegation ('golden showers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, analysts should quantify confidence or likelihood (even approximate ranges) for reported assertions to communicate uncertainty transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using reporting as investigatory roadmap vs. proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports indicated the FBI and Senate Intelligence Committee were 'using the dossier as a roadmap' for investigations, i.e., to guide lines of inquiry rather than as definitive proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat raw reporting as a potential roadmap to identify subjects, dates, and connections to investigate; ensure subsequent investigatory work seeks independent verification rather than relying on the roadmap itself as evidence.
